issues.description: IdentityGrammar admits unary sign on unsigned literals without specifying which signs the postcondition forbids.
issues.detail: The grammar now accepts an optional SignedSegmentGrammar before each numeric. There is no stated invariant about whether '+' is permitted on the seed, nor whether '--2' (double sign) is rejected. The author should state the postcondition: exactly one optional leading minus, no plus, no whitespace ambiguity. TESTED-NOT-PROVED: one fixture with -2147483648 is not a proof.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no cited precondition justifying it.
issues.detail: The PR description lists only 'non-quoted identifier' for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, yet the code also adds NumericLiteralSegment. Either the specification is wrong or the change is unmotivated. Neither test fixture exercises the numeric branch. State the precondition (T-SQL allows LCID integer?) or remove the alternative. UNREASONED as written.

issues.description: Removal of the multi-action ALTER TABLE example silently narrows accepted grammar without proof the prior form is invalid.
issues.detail: The diff deletes 'ALTER TABLE ... ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c' and calls it 'invalid.' T-SQL does in fact permit a single ADD followed by comma-delimited drops via the prior Delimited(OneOf(...)) construction is debated; the commit asserts invalidity without citation. Provide the BNF reference or restore the case.

issues.description: Replacing Delimited(OneOf(...)) with bare OneOf(...) loses the ability to compose multiple top-level alter actions in one statement.
issues.detail: Previously the outer Delimited allowed 'ALTER TABLE T ADD x INT, DROP COLUMN y'. The new shape only permits one action plus internal Delimited inside ADD/DROP. The postcondition has changed silently. If this matches T-SQL grammar, state it; if not, this is a regression masked by a fixture deletion.

issues.description: New DROP CONSTRAINT delimited form permits a syntactically pathological mixed list with optional 'CONSTRAINT' keyword per element.
issues.detail: The inner Sequence makes 'CONSTRAINT' optional per item, so 'DROP CONSTRAINT a, b, CONSTRAINT c' parses. The invariant 'every element is a constraint reference' holds, but the grammar admits inconsistent surface forms not documented in MS spec. Tighten or document.

issues.description: PR description contains 'DEFAULT_LANUGE' typo; minor but indicative of unreviewed prose accompanying grammar changes.
issues.detail: A misspelling in the change description is a small signal that the artifact was submitted without a final read-through. Correctness reviewers should treat this as a weak prior that the rest also wants careful re-reading. Cosmetic, but worth fixing before merge.

review.summary: The PR extends TSQL grammar in four areas but states no preconditions, postconditions, or invariants for the new productions. The restructure of AlterTableStatementSegment from Delimited(OneOf(...)) to a bare OneOf silently narrows what a single ALTER TABLE may express, and the simultaneous deletion of a multi-action fixture conceals whether this is a deliberate spec tightening or a regression. The identity-seed and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE changes admit broader inputs than the description claims, with no fixture exercising the new branches. TESTED-NOT-PROVED throughout: the YAML hashes change, no reasoning accompanies the structural choices. Acceptable after the author states which T-SQL surface each grammar rule is intended to admit and reject, and adds the missing fixtures.
